title: The three-year truth
intro: Small-cap funds: −13.2% this year, −7.8% over one year. Now the number the rally hid.
prompt: After the slump, what is the small-cap category's THREE-YEAR return (% per year)? For reference: a liquid fund earned ~6–7% a year over the same period.
debrief: 5.5% a year — LESS than a liquid fund over the same three years. That's the whole risk-premium lesson in one number: three years of small-cap volatility, drawdowns and headlines, paid less than parking the money. It isn't an argument against small caps forever — it's the argument for sizing them as a satellite you can hold through exactly this, and for deep suspicion whenever a hot trailing return is doing the selling.
